records.quote: Example 4.2. Let Ui ∼ q − W(q, λi, β) and Vi ∼ q − W(q, λ*i, β) for i = 1, 2 be two sets of components being mutually dependent with the Clayton copula (member of the Archimedean copula family). Here, we have considered the generators of the Clayton copula as ψ1(u) = 1/(1−u) and ψ2(u) = 1/√(2u+1). Then ϕ1(u) = (1−u)/u and ϕ2(u) = (1−u²)/(2u²). It is easy to verify that ψ1 and ψ2 are log-convex and ϕ2 ◦ ψ1 is super-additive. Set λ1 = 0.3, λ2 = 1.7, λ★1 = 0.5, λ★2 = 1.6, β = 0.5 and q = 0.5, then Figure 8(a) demonstrates that FUn:n − FVn:n ≤ 0 on (0, D) = (0, 1.384) when 0 < q < 1.

records.quote: For the case of 1 < q < 2, to model the dependence, we employ the Gumbel-Hougaard copula (member of Archimedean copula family) with generators ψ1(u) = e^{1−(1+u)^8} and ψ2(u) = e^{1−(1+u)^3}. Then ϕ1(u) = (1 − ln u)^{1/8} − 1 and ϕ2(u) = (1 − ln u)^{1/3} − 1. Observe that both ψ1(u) and ψ2(u) are log-concave and ϕ2 ◦ ψ1 is super-additive. With the parameter choices λ1 = 0.5, λ2 = 0.8, λ★1 = 0.3, λ★2 = 0.9, β = 0.5, and q = 1.5, Figure 9(b) demonstrates that the result also holds for 1 < q < 2.
